USA TODAY Co., Inc. is a diversified media company with expansive reach at the national and local level dedicated to empowering and enriching communities. We seek to inspire, inform, and connect audiences as a sustainable, growth focused media and digital marketing solutions company. Through our trusted brands, including the USA TODAY NETWORK, comprised of the national publication, USA TODAY, and local media organizations, including our network of local properties, in the United States, and Newsquest, a wholly-owned subsidiary operating in the United Kingdom, we provide essential journalism, local content, and digital experiences to audiences and businesses. We deliver high-quality, trusted content with a commitment to balanced, unbiased journalism, where and when consumers want to engage. Our digital marketing solutions brand, LocaliQ, supports small and medium-sized businesses with innovative digital marketing products and solutions. USA TODAY Co. open roles are featured on various external job boards. When applying to a position at USA TODAY Co., you should be completing an application on USA TODAY Co. Careers via Dayforce. Job postings directing you to complete an application on other external sites may not be valid. If you are a California resident, you acknowledge that by applying for a job with us, this California Job Applicant Privacy Notice will apply to our collection, use, and disclosure of your personal information. To connect with us, visit www.usatodayco.com

As a Database Engineer, you will help operate and improve the database systems that power LOCALiQ, running primarily in the cloud across MySQL, PostgreSQL, and BigQuery. You will partner closely with software engineers, data engineers, analysts, and data scientists to keep our data platforms fast, safe, and available as our products scale.

This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who is curious about data challenges, comfortable operating production systems, and motivated to automate the work that shouldn't be done by hand. You'll have the support of a senior team while owning meaningful pieces of the platform yourself.

We are a fast-paced, product-led engineering organization building the next generation of digital marketing management systems in partnership with Google, Bing, Yahoo, Facebook, and Snap. If you are technical, analytical, and eager to build solutions that directly impact the business, we want to talk to you.

What You'll Do

· Design, build, and operate database systems on MySQL, PostgreSQL, and BigQuery, primarily on Google Cloud Platform.

· Maintain performance, availability, and security across LOCALiQ's production database estate.

· Ensure data safety and data integrity, including backup, recovery, and disaster recovery validation.

· Perform routine database operations such as upgrades, patching, schema changes, replication management, and capacity planning.

· Tune and troubleshoot slow queries, blocking, and replication issues alongside application teams.

· Review database changes to minimize deployment risk, and help teams design schemas and access patterns that scale.

· Automate recurring operational work through scripting, infrastructure as code, and CI/CD pipelines.

· Participate in a scheduled 24x7 on-call rotation shared with other team members.

Required Skills

· 3+ years of experience in a Database Engineer, Database Administrator, or similar role.

· Hands-on experience managing production database infrastructure in a cloud environment (GCP, AWS, or Azure).

· Working knowledge of relational databases — MySQL and/or PostgreSQL — including administration, replication, and backup/recovery.

· Strong SQL skills, including the ability to read, write, and optimize non-trivial queries.

· Programming experience in at least one language — Python preferred, but Go, Java, Ruby, or similar are all valuable.

· Experience with Git version control and working on code as part of a team.

· Sound judgment around change management, risk, and data integrity in production systems.

· BS or MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

· Curiosity, self-direction, and a bias toward automating repetitive work.

Preferred Skills

· Experience with Google Cloud Platform, particularly Cloud SQL, BigQuery, GKE, and Pub/Sub (equivalent AWS experience with RDS, Redshift, EKS, and SQS is welcome).

· Experience with BigQuery or another cloud data warehouse, including cost and performance optimization.

· Experience data modeling and data transformation tools like Dataform or DBT

· Experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform), containers, and CI/CD practices such as test automation and automated deployments.

· Comfort working in an Agile/Scrum environment.

· Exposure to digital marketing or online advertising data (SEO/SEM) is an advantage.

#LI-NR2

job.title: Product Marketing Manager
job.description:
Product Marketing Manager, Events 

Austin, Texas | Full-Time

Build the Events Austin Talks About.

Some people market events. Some people live them.

We're looking for someone who wants to immerse themselves in Hearst Austin Media’s event culture and help grow some of the most recognized experiential brands in Central Texas.

This role will serve as the marketing lead for our portfolio of wellness, lifestyle, food, music, and community events, with a primary focus on the Cap10K, Texas' largest 10K and one of Austin's most iconic traditions.

We're looking for someone who wants to be on the course, behind the scenes, at packet pickup, at community runs, at merchandise launches, talking to participants, interviewing runners, capturing content, trying a two-step and weighing in on which burger delights the senses. We need a builder of community and help shaping what these event brands become next.

If you've ever thought, "I wish I could get paid to be obsessed with Austin events," this might be your dream job.

 

What You'll Do

Be the Voice of the Brand

You'll help tell the story of our events year-round through social media, video, email, digital campaigns and community activations.

You'll interview participants, capture content in the field, showcase event experiences and help audiences feel connected long before race day or event day arrives.

Grow Participation

You'll develop marketing campaigns that drive registrations, ticket sales, attendance, merchandise purchases and repeat participation.

You'll understand who our audiences are, what motivates them and what inspires them to become lifelong fans.

Be Embedded in the Experience

You'll work closely with our Race Director, event producers, creative team and operations leaders. You'll attend planning meetings, community activations, training runs, sponsor events, merchandise launches and race-weekend activities.

You should expect to spend time where the action is happening.

Turn Merch into a Movement

We're investing in merchandise as part of the participant experience.

You'll help launch products, create campaigns, build anticipation and turn our merchandise program into something audiences actively seek out.

Build Community

You'll develop relationships with running clubs, fitness groups, creators, community organizations, local businesses and cultural influencers who help make Austin special.

We want our events to feel like they're built with the community, not simply marketed to it.

 

You'll Thrive Here If...

You love Austin.

You know what's happening around town before everyone else does.

You naturally take photos and videos at events.

You have opinions about race shirts, medals, event experiences and social content.

You enjoy being around people.

You can comfortably walk up to someone, hand them a microphone and get a great story.

You think community is created one interaction at a time.

You get excited about building something bigger every year.

 

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of marketing, audience development, events, experiential marketing, community engagement or related experience
  • Strong social media and content creation skills
  • Comfortable appearing on camera and interviewing participants
  • Experience building campaigns that drive registrations, attendance, purchases or subscriptions
  • Strong project management and organizational skills
  • Ability to work evenings and weekends as events require
  • Passion for live experiences and community-building

 

Bonus Points

  • You're a runner.
  • You've worked in sports, wellness, fitness, hospitality, festivals or live events.
  • You've helped launch merchandise programs.
  • You're already active in Austin's running, fitness or event communities.
  • You have video creation and storytelling experience.

 

What Success Looks Like

A year from now:

  • More people are participating in our events.
  • More people are wearing our merchandise.
  • Our social channels feel alive.
  • Austin sees our brands as part of the community.
  • Participants feel like they're part of something bigger than a single event.

 

Most importantly, when someone thinks about the best events in Austin, they think about the brands you've helped build.

About the Austin American-Statesman:

The Austin American-Statesman (statesman.com) has been the leading source of news and information for Central Texas since 1871, serving a dynamic and fast-growing region anchored by the capital city of Texas. Austin is known for its vibrant tech industry, rich cultural heritage, influential government institutions and creative spirit. Since its acquisition by Hearst in 2025, the Statesman continues to operate with editorial independence while benefiting from Hearst’s expansive journalistic and technological resources.

About Hearst Newspapers:

The Austin American-Statesman is a division of Hearst Newspapers (HNP). With 2,500 employees across the nation, HNP represents a network of 24 daily and 52 weekly publications, including the San Francisco Chronicle, Houston Chronicle, San Antonio Express-News and Albany Times Union, marketing services businesses, and entertainment businesses such as King Features Syndicate. At HNP, we are investing in new and innovative ways to tell stories – growing newsrooms, diversifying tools, evolving platforms – to support the millions of people who trust us each month to help them make decisions, take action and be inspired. Be a part of something bigger – Your Headline Awaits.

job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Instructions

  • Application Deadline: Friday, October 2nd at 12pm ET.

  • Submission Instructions: Please submit a cover letter in addition to your resume, including related clips you are proud of.

Intro to Position

NPR’s award-winning Politics & Policy Desk delivers sophisticated, accessible coverage of the White House, Congress, the Supreme Court, the Department of Justice, national security, and the intersection of technology and political power. Our journalism is grounded in original reporting, breaking news delivered with context, and clear explanatory storytelling. Our work reaches millions of listeners and readers daily across Morning Edition, All Things Considered, NPR.org, Up First, and the NPR Politics Podcast.

The Justice Department Correspondent leads NPR’s daily and enterprise coverage of the Department of Justice, federal law enforcement, and federal immigration jurisprudence and prosecutions. Based in Washington, D.C., this reporter is responsible for breaking significant news, cultivating institutional and frontline sources, and delivering analytical enterprise reporting that reveals how DOJ decisions impact governance, the rule of law, and communities across the country.

The Politics & Policy Desk operates across audio, digital, and visual platforms. The correspondent evaluates the optimal narrative format for each story—whether an investigative data analysis, a live two-way on broadcast newsmagazines, an episode of the NPR Politics Podcast, or an explanatory digital feature.

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with SAG-AFTRA.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.

Responsibilities

Reporting & Enterprise Journalism

  • Pitches, reports, and produces high-impact daily news spots, contextual enterprise pieces, and investigative stories on the Department of Justice, immigration enforcement, and federal legal policy.
  • Cultivates and maintains diverse, reliable source networks across government agencies, legal institutions, advocacy organizations, and impacted communities.
  • Analyzes complex court filings, regulatory decisions, and legislative proposals to deliver accurate, timely explanatory journalism.

Multiplatform Collaboration & Production

  • Delivers live, unscripted reporting and conversational analysis on NPR newsmagazines (Morning Edition, All Things Considered), breaking news specials, podcasts, and member station programming.
  • Partners with desk editors, audio producers, and digital editors to package reporting effectively for broadcast, digital text, and multimedia platforms.
  • Gathers audio in the field, conducts recorded interviews, and assists in the editorial editing and audio production of pieces under tight deadlines.

Editorial Standards & Administration

  • Maintains absolute adherence to the NPR Ethics Handbook, legal standards, and factual accuracy guidelines across all platforms.
  • Completes essential administrative duties accurately and punctually, including source documentation, program summaries, assignment coordination, and travel/expense filing.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • At least 5 years of professional journalism experience reporting on complex legal, governmental, or regulatory affairs at a national or regional level.
  • Demonstrated track record of reporting and writing accurate, contextual enterprise stories and breaking news on deadline.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and sustain professional source networks across institutional, agency, and community settings.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple overlapping stories and shifting deadlines with editorial sound judgment.
  • Proven ability to collaborate effectively within a fast-moving newsroom team, showing consistent respect for colleagues, diverse perspectives, and public radio member stations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proven beat-reporting experience covering the U.S. Department of Justice, federal courts, or federal immigration enforcement.
  • Experience communicating complex policy, legal, or political topics clearly and conversationally for broadcast, podcast, or live audio formats.
  • Established record of enterprise scoops and investigative reporting derived from original document analysis and agency sourcing.
  • Experience producing multiplatform content, including digital written features, podcast appearances, and visual/social explainers.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and work experience.

Work Location & Requirements

  • Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. The employee will be required to be in the office in Washington, D.C., or at an on-site reporting location at least 3 days a week. The employee must also reside in Washington, D.C., Maryland, or Virginia.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range : The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $127,500 - $142,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

Personal Service Contract (PSC) Eligibility: This role is eligible for a Personal Service Contract (PSC). A PSC is an individualized agreement between NPR and a SAG-AFTRA represented employee that provides enhanced base compensation and tailored employment terms. In exchange for this higher guaranteed pay and added flexibility, employees on a PSC waive eligibility for premium pay (such as holiday or travel premiums) and compensatory time that are otherwise provided under the SAG-AFTRA collective bargaining agreement.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

job.title: Licensing Senior Account Manager
job.description:
About ASCAP

The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) is a membership association of more than one million songwriters, composers and music publishers, and represents some of the world’s most talented music creators. Founded and governed by songwriters, composers and publishers, it is the only performing rights organization in the U.S. that operates on a not-for-profit basis. ASCAP licenses a repertory of over 20 million musical works to hundreds of thousands of businesses that use music, including streaming services, cable television, radio and satellite radio and brick and mortar businesses such as retail stores, hotels, clubs, restaurants and bars. ASCAP collects the licensing fees; identifies, matches and processes trillions of performances every year; and returns nearly 90 cents of every dollar back to its members as royalties. The ASCAP blanket license offers an efficient solution for businesses to legally perform ASCAP music while respecting the right of songwriters and composers to be paid fairly. ASCAP puts music creators first, advocating for their rights and the value of music on Capitol Hill, driving innovation that moves the industry forward, building community and providing the resources and support that creators need to succeed in their careers. Learn more and stay in touch at www.ascap.com, on X and Instagram @ASCAP and on Facebook.

# # #

Job Overview:

The Licensing Senior Account Manager is responsible for driving new business and growing revenue by effectively communicating the need for and the benefits of an ASCAP license agreement to prospective new customers, closing deals with such customers as well as maintaining account relationships and concluding renewal deals with existing customers.

The Licensing Senior Account Manager will communicate and collaborate with the Senior and Associate Directors, SVPs and work cross-functionally with others within the Licensing Department (e.g., Operations, Reactive, Customer Service). Additionally, they will work closely with other departments such as Business and Legal Affairs, Revenue Accounting, Distribution, and Global Technology Solutions.

Areas of Responsibility & Accountability:

  • Identify, assess, and drive licensing efforts by generating and converting leads into both new license prospects and “click-through” licensees
  • Negotiate with select prospective new customers, answering questions, following up and remaining engaged until deal closure
  • Manage select accounts by answering customer queries, resolving issues and pursuing outstanding items
  • Develop, maintain and strengthen relationships among licensee accounts
  • Escalate matters/issues to senior team members when prescribed processes meet impediments and/or when otherwise necessary or appropriate
  • Perform as the backup to the Licensing Business Analyst, gathering and disseminating news and business intelligence to ASCAP leadership when they are not available

Qualifications & Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; music industry studies a plus
  • Ability to work independently with guidance from senior team members
  • A minimum of three years of sales, business development and/or customer service experience, preferably in the music and/or media industry
  • Ability to effectively engage in revenue-generating activities to contribute to ASCAP’s revenue goals
  • Ability to clearly and concisely explain detailed subject matter (i.e. ASCAP and the need/benefits of an ASCAP license) to prospective customers
  • Knowledge of music/copyright, entertainment and technology industries preferred
  • Ability to foresee and stay apprised of new licensing opportunities (i.e. products, services, platforms), particularly those utilizing new/emerging technologies, and the ability to synthesize this information into high-quality formats (emails, reports, PowerPoint) for presentation to senior management
  • Proficiency with Salesforce and/or other CRMs preferred
  • Ability to work cross-functionally on multi-faceted projects
  • Ability to take direction and self-motivate; drive to master core responsibilities and to help a team maximize production and achieve goals
  • Excellent organizational, verbal and written communication skills; professional demeanor; ability to interact effectively with all levels of management and external personnel
  • Excellent attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to meet deadlines under pressure
  • Proven ability to multitask, assess and shift priorities around as needed
  • Ability to work well both individually and on a team while sharing pertinent information, supporting colleagues, and encouraging participation
  • This position requires three days per week in the New York office

Compensation/Benefits:

Besides providing a unique and dynamic work environment, there are a few other reasons you should consider ASCAP in your career planning. We also offer generous benefit options that are comprehensive and provide the flexibility that most employees want and need. These health care and financial plan options include the following:

  • A choice of either network-only provider medical and dental plans or more flexible medical and dental plans where you can see providers in or out-of-network
  • Vision plan that offers both in and out-of-network provider options
  • 401(k) Plan that offers pre-tax, Roth, and an after-tax employee contribution option which includes a company match
  • An additional employer paid discretionary profit share contribution, regardless of your participation in the 401(k) Plan
  • Generous time-off policy
  • Health care and dependent care flexible spending accounts
  • Short-term disability insurance/salary continuation and long-term disability insurance
  • Company provided basic life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance
  • Employee gym discounts at select gyms
  • Commuter benefits
  • Voluntary pet health insurance
  • Voluntary auto and homeowner’s insurance
  • Voluntary employee, spouse, and dependent life insurance options
  • Voluntary ID protection Coverage

The above summary of the current benefits is subject to the terms and conditions of the benefit plan documents. This summary is not complete and is subject to the terms of the underlying plan documents. Please note that ASCAP reserves the right to amend or otherwise revise or terminate, at any time and in its sole discretion, its benefit plans, programs, and policies.

Occasional travel for in-person meetings may be required.

The anticipated base salary range for this position is $80,000 to $87,000 and will be determined on an individualized basis depending on several factors that are unique to each candidate including geographic location (due to differences in the cost of labor), skills, education and prior relevant experience.

job.title: Senior Manager, Platform Engineering and Delivery
job.description:
Who We Are:
SiriusXM and its brands (Pandora, SiriusXM Media, AdsWizz, Simplecast, and SiriusXM Connect) are leading a new era of audio entertainment and services by delivering the most compelling subscription and ad-supported audio entertainment experience for listeners -- in the car, at home, and anywhere on the go with connected devices. Our vision is to shape the future of audio, where everyone can be effortlessly connected to the voices, stories and music they love wherever they are.
 

This is the place where a diverse group of emerging talent and legends alike come to share authentic and purposeful songs, stories, sounds and insights through some of the best programming and technology in the world. Our critically acclaimed, industry-leading audio entertainment encompasses music, sports, comedy, news, talk, live events, and podcasting. No matter their individual role, each of our employees plays a vital part in bringing SiriusXM’s vision to life every day.
 

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, and the premier programmer and platform for subscription and digital advertising-supported audio products. SiriusXM’s platforms collectively reach approximately 150 million listeners, the largest digital audio audience across paid and free tiers in North America, and deliver music, sports, talk, news, comedy, entertainment and podcasts. Pandora, a subsidiary of SiriusXM, is the largest ad-supported audio entertainment streaming service in the U.S. SiriusXM's subsidiaries Simplecast and AdsWizz make it a leader in podcast hosting, production, distribution, analytics and monetization. The Company’s advertising sales organization, which operates as SiriusXM Media, leverages its scale, cross-platform sales organization and ad tech capabilities to deliver results for audio creators and advertisers. SiriusXM, through SiriusXM Canada Holdings, Inc., also offers satellite radio and audio entertainment in Canada. In addition to its audio entertainment businesses, SiriusXM offers connected vehicle services to automakers.

How you’ll make an impact:
As Senior Manager, Platform Engineering & Delivery, you will lead multiple delivery capability domains within Platform Engineering focused on improving software delivery across SiriusXM. You will be accountable for the teams, technical leads, shared platforms, and operating standards engineering organizations rely on to develop, validate, secure, package, and release software at scale. In this role, you will define and execute the annual and multi-year delivery engineering strategy and roadmap, ensuring that our platforms and tools measurably improve developer productivity, software quality, operational consistency, release reliability, adoption, and security posture. You will establish shared engineering standards and governance, influence senior leaders across engineering, infrastructure, security, and product, and make investment, staffing, and prioritization decisions that build a strong organization and develop future leaders.

What you’ll do:

  • Lead Organization and Roadmap: Lead multiple delivery capability domains and the engineers and technical leads responsible for them. Own the annual and multi-year roadmap for platform investments, establish priorities and success measures, and align capacity, staffing, vendor, and tooling decisions with Platform Engineering leadership and senior stakeholders.

  • Drive Strategy and Execution for Core Delivery Capabilities: Direct the strategy, tooling, and execution across CI/CD, artifact management, production containers, code quality, and security scanning, with a focus on specific outcomes:

    • Accelerating Delivery: Improve development speed, release reliability, and consistency across teams through CI/CD tooling and shared components.

    • Standardizing Artifacts and Containers: Ensure software packages, build outputs, and containerized workloads are reliable, traceable, secure, and standardized for easy consumption and delivery.

    • Improving Quality and Security Posture: Drive capabilities for code quality and security scanning to enhance maintainability, engineering effectiveness, and enable secure-by-default delivery practices by shifting security earlier in the development lifecycle.

  • Foster Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner closely with security, infrastructure, developer experience, and application engineering teams to identify friction, improve workflows, and deliver scalable shared solutions.

  • Operational Accountability and Excellence: Own technical and organizational decision-making for the delivery engineering portfolio, ensuring solutions align with broader platform strategy and business goals. Set priorities across multiple concurrent efforts, resolve cross-functional trade-offs, and manage material risks, dependencies, service reliability, capacity, and investment decisions.

  • Performance, Standards, and Governance: Establish and evolve engineering processes, delivery standards, governance, and secure-by-default practices. Use adoption, developer productivity, delivery performance, reliability, quality, and security metrics to evaluate platform effectiveness and hold teams accountable for measurable operational outcomes.

  • Develop Talent and Organizational Capability: Coach and develop technical leads and engineers, build a strong leadership bench, and create succession and development plans. Partner with Talent Acquisition and HR on hiring, organization design, workforce planning, performance management, and staffing decisions across the delivery engineering portfolio.

  • Enterprise Adoption and Executive Influence: Drive adoption of shared delivery platforms and standards across multiple engineering organizations. Present recommendations, performance results, risks, and investment trade-offs to senior management and secure alignment on changes that affect company-wide software delivery.

  • Resource and Vendor Stewardship: Plan and manage the team’s operating capacity and approved tooling or vendor investments, balancing cost, reliability, security, and developer experience while ensuring resources are aligned to strategic priorities.

What you’ll need:

  • Typically has 7 or more years of experience with 3 or more years of management experience managing software engineering teams, including responsibility for multiple capability areas, technical leads, or managers, and demonstrated success developing leadership talent.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Domain Expertise: Experience with one or more core delivery domains: CI/CD systems, artifact repositories, container platforms, code quality tooling, software supply chain controls, or security scanning platforms.

  • Strategic & Technical Judgment: Strong technical judgment and understanding of modern software delivery architecture, with the ability to challenge technical decisions, assess risk, and guide complex trade-offs. Demonstrated ability to contribute to engineering strategy, improve processes, and align execution with business priorities.

  • Team and People Leadership: Experience leading multiple engineering capability areas and delivering results across complex, cross-organizational technical initiatives. Strong people leadership skills encompassing coaching and mentoring senior engineers, technical leads, and managers; performance management; succession planning; talent development; team building; and organization design.

  • Operational Excellence and Communication: Strong organizational and operational leadership skills, including annual and multi-year planning, portfolio prioritization, execution management, service accountability, risk mitigation, capacity planning, and vendor or tooling investment decisions.

  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and executive-influence skills, with demonstrated ability to align technical and non-technical stakeholders, resolve sensitive cross-functional trade-offs, and gain adoption of shared standards across multiple engineering organizations.

  • Experience using automation, AI-assisted development tools, or workflow optimization to improve delivery efficiency and engineering productivity is a plus.

  • Must have legal right to work in the U.S.

At SiriusXM, we carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including your background and experience. These considerations can cause your compensation to vary. We expect the base salary for this position to be in the range of $106,600 to $190,000 and will depend on your skills, qualifications, and experience. job.description:

job.title: Head of Legal
job.description:
Who We Are

UnitedMasters is building a marketplace that connects artists, brands and fans - empowering artists to earn and grow. UnitedMasters has taken the bold step of building a music distribution service that, radically, puts artists first - disrupting the legacy music business by letting up-and-coming artists distribute their music directly to fans through streaming services while maintaining ownership of their master recording rights and up to 100% of royalties. Through the combination of UnitedMasters’ music distribution platform and its deep ties to brands, UnitedMasters enables independent artists and change-makers to grow and earn unlike any other platform.

The UnitedMasters team is made up of musicians, marketers, engineers, and storytellers with backgrounds from YouTube, SoundCloud, Pandora, Facebook, Uber, Dropbox, Complex, VICE, and more. We work hand in hand with the award-winning creative teams that forge those innovative partnerships at Translation (our in-house creative advertising agency).

We are looking for a Head of Legal to join UnitedMasters! This role is for a strategic, business-minded legal leader who thrives at the intersection of music, technology, and advertising. In this role, you’ll serve as a key partner to executive leadership, advising on risk, commercial transactions, corporate strategy, and high-impact partnerships across UnitedMasters LLC and Translation LLC. You’ll play a critical role in shaping the company’s legal and business direction while leading and developing the legal team. This is an opportunity for someone who can think big, move decisively, and help guide the company through its next phase of growth.

This role is based in Brooklyn, New York with four days in-office and one day remote.


What You'll Do

  • Partner directly with the C-suite and senior leadership to provide strategic legal guidance and risk analysis on key initiatives and company direction.
  • Structure and advise on complex commercial arrangements, including distribution, licensing, partnerships, and strategic transactions.
  • Serve as a senior legal advisor across the full enterprise, including music distribution, product and technology, international expansion, sync and licensing, corporate strategy, business development, advertising, and supporting shared services (HR, Finance, IT).
  • Manage the internal legal team, setting priorities, allocating resources, and elevating overall legal function performance.
  • Partner and coordinate with outside counsel, ensuring efficient execution, cost management, and alignment with company objectives.
  • Lead development and implementation of scalable legal frameworks, policies, and best practices across the organization
  • Guide product, technology, and international teams on launches, expansion, and regulatory considerations
  • Oversee and manage enforcing rights, dispute resolution strategy, including pre-litigation, litigation, and settlement approach.
  • Ensure the company operates with a practical, business-forward legal posture that enables growth rather than restricts it

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Background in IP, media, technology, music and/or entertainment law, with strong commercial instincts.
  • Proven ability to operate at a strategic level, advising executives and influencing business outcomes while maintaining strong relationships internally and externally.
  • Experience managing or leading legal teams and partnering with outside counsel.
  • Deep understanding of commercial deal structures, rights frameworks, and global business operations.
  • Strong judgment, with the ability to balance legal risk against business objectives.
  • Effective communicator, excellent writer, and outward leader who can translate complex legal concepts into clear, actionable guidance.
  • Comfortable operating cross-functionally with product, finance, HR, marketing, and business teams.
  • Proficiency with AI-powered legal tools and workflows (e.g., contract review/analysis, legal research, and document automation), with the ability to leverage emerging technologies to improve legal efficiency, scalability, and decision-making.

Minimum Qualifications

  • J.D. from an accredited law school, admitted and in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction, preferably NY.
  • 8 to 15 years of experience, with a mix of reputable entertainment law firm and in-house experience

About UnitedMasters, Inc.

UnitedMasters Inc. represents the creative solutions company, Translation, and the leading software and services platform for independent creators, UnitedMasters. UnitedMasters enables ownership, exposure, and new paths for financial return for independent creators, while Translation helps brands leverage the power of contemporary culture to achieve transformational growth. Combined, UnitedMasters, Inc. is the world’s leading marketplace for cultural capital, connecting independent artists and brands to realize a future in which all creators own their future. Backed by Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz, and Apple, UnitedMasters, Inc. is reimagining how brands and artists come together to tell their stories, build profitable growth, and push culture forward.

Salary Hiring Range: $220,000 - $300,000

job.description:
About the Team:

The Print Team supports the end-to-end lifecycle of Dow Jones’ print publications—including The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, Investor’s Business Daily, and the New York Post.

Operating across ad intake, production workflows, plant operations, printing, packaging, single copy and amenity sales, Reprints and Licensing, and distribution; the team collaborates with internal cross-functional partners and external vendors, distributors, and the USPS to ensure quality, content freshness, safety, and cost efficiency from creation to final delivery.

About the Role:

The Mechanic provides mechanic maintenance support to plant operations. The ability to perform work safely, meet the needs of operations, execute the maintenance program and comply with all safety codes is paramount. You will identify, troubleshoot and repair problems in mechanical systems that occur in production equipment. You will run tests, isolate problems, remove/replace failed components, determine failure modes by studying worn components and perform other tasks while also performing preventive maintenance and upgrades to mechanical systems. You will be based on-site at our Print Plant reporting to the Machinist Foreman.

You Will:

  • Perform preventive maintenance on mechanical systems to include disassembly, cleaning, reassembly, and calibration. Act on information obtained from operators to diagnose equipment problems. Clean, lubricate, and adjust parts, equipment, and machinery.

  • Disassemble machinery and equipment to remove parts and make repairs. Examine parts for defects such as breakage and excessive wear. Observe and test the operation of machinery and equipment to diagnose malfunctions, using voltmeters and other testing devices. Operate newly repaired machinery and equipment to verify the adequacy of repairs. Reassemble equipment after completion of inspections, testing, or repairs. Repair and maintain the operating condition of industrial production machinery and equipment. Repair and replace broken or malfunctioning components of machinery and equipment.

  • Study blueprints and manufacturer manuals to determine correct installation and operation of machinery. Cuts and welds metal to repair broken metal parts, fabricate new parts, and assemble new equipment. Test all repairs upon completion.

  • Record parts and materials used, and request new parts and materials. Record repairs and maintenance performed. Sometimes repairs or modifications are performed when blueprints and manufacturer specifications are unavailable or incomplete.

  • Utilize safety and security practices and procedures following established rules and regulations and maintain a safe, clean, and secure work environment.

  • Communicate with management, mechanics, and equipment operators to advise them if there are any potential mechanical hazards. Execute the maintenance work schedule as provided by your supervisor. This will require strategic decisions to ensure the scheduled work will be completed within the period scheduled.

  • Keep the Foreman informed of all issues which may affect the operational capability of the equipment.

  • Ensure the shop is maintained in a safe and orderly fashion. Attend meetings and support continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Maintain close contact with the Foreman, maintenance crew, the production supervisors and equipment operators. Keep the maintenance supervisor and manager informed on all abnormal or critical situations and seek advice on matters outside of their knowledge or authority. Perform other tasks and special assignments as requested by management. Work with the production manager to set equipment maintenance priorities.

  • Rotate shifts as scheduled by the plant management. The primary production hours of the plant are after 5pm (second shift). This is a rotating shift between 1st and 2nd shift with other team members with some weekend work required.

You Have:

  • High school degree or 1- 3 years of equivalent experience in industrial / commercial mechanics preferred.

  • Knowledge of basic mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and electrical systems and safe machine operation principles including welding experience.

  • Capability of lifting press parts and making mechanical repairs.

  • Good math, mechanical, organizational, written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to stand for extended periods, bend, stoop, reach, and lift 35-pounds.

job.title: Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting
job.description:
About the Role:

As Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting, you will lead Dow Jones Energy's global chemicals price reporting business. You will oversee the editorial teams responsible for the assessment and publication of benchmark prices, assessments and market-moving news across global petrochemical and chemical markets from our PCW brand.

You ensure the integrity, quality, transparency, and market relevance of chemical price assessments while maintaining the highest ethical and methodological standards. You will lead a global team of price reporters and editors responsible for market coverage across key chemical value chains - including aromatics, olefins, plastics, polymers, syngas, methanol, feedstocks, and emerging chemical markets.

You will drive editorial excellence, benchmark innovation, and market engagement, while ensuring compliance with legal requirements and industry standards. You will partner closely with Product, Standards & Compliance, Risk, and other Editorial leaders to ensure Dow Jones Energy's chemicals assessments remain trusted, transparent, and indispensable to global commodity markets.

You will report to the SVP - Markets & Price Reporting.

About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.

Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.

You Will:

  • Lead and develop a global team of chemicals price reporters, editors, and market specialists, fostering a culture of editorial excellence, accountability, and collaboration

  • Ensure all chemical market assessments are developed, maintained, and published in accordance with the highest standards of price assessment integrity, market transparency, governance, and ethical conduct consistent with Dow Jones’ and The Wall Street Journal’s values

  • Lead methodology development, periodic methodology reviews, market consultations, and stakeholder engagement processes to ensure pricing methodologies remain robust, representative, and responsive to evolving market dynamics

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with producers, consumers, traders, brokers, exchanges, trade associations, and other market participants to strengthen market engagement, data integrity, and confidence in Dow Jones Energy's petrochemical and chemical markets assessments

  • Partner with Standards & Compliance, Legal, and Risk teams to ensure ongoing compliance with applicable benchmark regulations, internal controls, audit requirements, and governance frameworks

  • Partner with Product to execute the strategic roadmap for global chemicals market coverage, including identifying opportunities for new benchmarks, market expansion, and portfolio optimization

  • Monitor benchmark performance, market adoption, customer feedback, and competitive developments - recommending changes to methodologies, coverage, and editorial priorities as appropriate

  • Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain high-performing editorial talent, ensuring appropriate succession planning, capability development, and organizational resilience across the chemicals price reporting organization

  • Act as a senior spokesperson and subject matter expert for chemicals markets, representing Dow Jones Energy at industry conferences, customer engagements, webinars, and regulatory forums

You Have:

  • 15+ years’ experience in commodity price reporting, market intelligence, or related information services organization

  • Deep knowledge of global chemicals and petrochemical markets, including physical market structures, trading practices, supply chains, and pricing mechanisms

  • Significant leadership experience managing geographically dispersed editorial, price reporting, or market analysis teams

  • Demonstrated experience developing, managing, or launching benchmark price assessments, methodologies, or market intelligence products

  • Strong understanding of IOSCO Principles for Oil Price Reporting Agencies and familiarity with benchmark regulation, governance, assurance, and audit requirements

  • Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to cultivate relationships with senior leaders and external market participants

  • A university degree -OR- relevant professional experience

The Dow Jones Printing Plant Apprenticeship Program is a 6-month immersive experience designed to give participants real exposure to how modern print operations work at the intersection of manufacturing and technology.

  • Support day-to-day production in a live printing environment

  • Monitor equipment and assist with preventive/predictive maintenance using a CMMS system

  • Work with Variable Data Printing (VDP) and digital pre-press processes

  • Explore tools to improve efficiency in layout and production workflows

  • Contribute to projects focused on sustainability, efficiency, or process improvement

  • Troubleshoot mechanical and system-related issues alongside experienced team members

  • Interest in manufacturing, engineering, or technical operations

  • Curiosity about how things work—both mechanically and digitally

Students interested in pursuing a career in manufacturing, engineering, or print operations. Dow Jones is on a mission to provide the world’s most trusted journalism, data and analysis to help people make decisions. As part of the company’s global communications team, the Corporate Communications Associate plays a key role in delivering a strategic, comprehensive communications playbook that leverages executive voices and key milestones to support the Dow Jones narrative and drive brand authority. Reporting to the Head of Client Retention, the Client Retention Director will assume responsibility for managing a team of Client Engagement Specialists (CES), with a strategic focus on retaining and nurturing Dow Jones’ professional business across the Americas within key Dow Jones Risk product verticals (Risk & Compliance + Knowledge & Insights).

Furthermore, the Director will collaborate closely with the product, operations, sales, and marketing teams on various initiatives critical to Dow Jones and its clientele.

The successful candidate must seamlessly integrate leadership acumen with strategic insights and will function as an integral part of the broader global retention team. This role requires ensuring the team consistently meets or surpasses retention targets and business objectives through the implementation of a layered client-centric approach.

You Will:

  • Team Leadership: Guide and support the CES team, establishing clear objectives and managing performance to achieve defined retention targets and onboarding/migration objectives. Serve as the primary escalation point for client issues, ensuring prompt and effective resolution. Ability to oversee a multi-layered organizational structure, leading managers and their teams to deliver against company goals.

  • Strategy: Design and execute region-specific retention strategies in alignment with the overarching global strategy, company goals, and client satisfaction imperatives. Structure long-term resource and personnel planning to ensure optimal client support and retention, concurrently building collaborative strategies with partners across Dow Jones in Operations, Product, Sales, and Marketing.

Foster inter-departmental collaboration to develop ongoing retention strategies and maximize customer satisfaction.

  • Sales Support, Growth & Collaboration: Offer strategic insight and support for new sales pursuits within existing client accounts, collaborating with Account Executives and Regional Sales Leaders to maximize customer Return on Investment (ROI) and expand revenue streams.

  • Collaborate with content strategy, product, social, multimedia and live journalism teams to seamlessly extend our direct relationships and community-building efforts both on- and off-platform.

  • Relentlessly advocate for the reader, ensuring every direct interaction delivers the expertise and value expected of the Journal.

You have:

  • 10+ years of experience in digital media with expertise in building communities and relationships between newsrooms and audiences.

  • A proven talent for leading, motivating and developing high-performing teams that drive substantial audience growth and subscriber loyalty.

  • A self-starter mentality, a flexible, can-do attitude and a passion for connecting with audiences.

job.description:
Experience Design Lead, Brand Marketing

Dow Jones and The Wall Street Journal are seeking a strategic and innovative Experience Design Lead to join our Brand Marketing team. This role focuses on enhancing user experience (UX), shaping customer journeys, and maintaining brand integrity across marketing touchpoints.

You’ll bridge strategy and execution, ensuring consistent, audience-first design across platforms and campaigns. Leading a small team with the Brand team, you’ll collaborate closely with Marketing, Subscription Strategy, Acquisition, Events, Design & Research, and Product to build cohesive, high-impact customer experiences across WSJ, WSJ+, and other Dow Jones brands.

This hands-on leadership role reports to the Brand Creative Director and combines UX & UI design expertise with brand stewardship. You’ll drive projects across teams, guide designers and partners, and ensure brand fidelity while meeting business goals.

Your role will involve collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality, audience-centric design solutions that drive engagement, loyalty, and conversion.

This is not a product design role. Instead, it’s a brand-led opportunity for a UX design generalist within a brand marketing context—connecting the dots across campaigns, platforms, and internal silos to build customer journeys that are both strategically sound and beautifully executed. The Experience Design Lead will play a crucial role in shaping the way our customers interact with our brands and surfaces.

Responsibilities & Activities

  • Lead UX / UI design and brand experience initiatives from within the Marketing org, partnering with cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Synthesize complex business goals into clear, actionable design strategies that result in refined user experiences and interfaces.

  • Drive customer journey mapping and experience strategy across acquisition, engagement, and retention touchpoints for WSJ, WSJ+, and Dow Jones brands.

  • Collaborate and align with Subscription Strategy, Acquisition and Events teams to translate business goals into UX objectives and audience-centric experiences, and define design briefs.

  • Understand and define project architecture from vision to execution, draft project roadmaps to build coalition and guide progress.

  • Deliver hands-on design: wireframes, user flows, UI, and visual assets—ensuring brand consistency and design excellence.

  • Incorporate AI tools to enhance efficiency and speed, without compromising quality

  • With your team, oversee the brand experience across touchpoints — connecting the dots, identifying gaps, and implementing cross functional design solutions.

  • Bridge Brand and Design & Research teams to integrate brand design standards and visual identities into UX design systems, working toward building a single source universal design standards for digital surfaces .

  • Guide and design UI to meet standards for brand consistency and visual design excellence.

  • Advocate for design-forward marketing UX foundations, improve design and user experience for existing websites and platforms, and innovate new solutions and UI patterns following best practices.

  • Refine existing customer journeys with a strategic, content-focused, design-forward, audience-first approach.

  • Ensure brand consistency, design and typographic excellence across all marketing efforts and customer journeys.

  • Guide and mentor a small team of designers, providing leadership across UX and UI design.

  • Review and provide directional feedback for the design and partner teams’ work, ensuring quality and standards and adherence to project and business objectives.

  • Manage designers and other resources to deliver projects on tight deadlines.

  • Educate stakeholders and colleagues to build understanding of UX best practices.

  • Share knowledge and inspire the team with knowledge of design and UX trends, and deep interest in the design landscape.

Qualifications & Criteria

  • 10+ years of experience in UX and brand design.

  • 4+ years in a lead or management role, directing cross functional teams on complex projects from concept through execution.

  • Strong process orientation and systems thinking—able to balance long-term brand vision with near-term tactical execution.

  • A passion for mentoring and developing design talent, especially in upskilling visual designers into well-rounded UI designers with strong UX foundations.

  • Strong understanding of how brand, UX, and marketing intersect to shape customer experience.

  • Proven ability to lead both strategic planning and design conversations and execute UX/UI design hands-on.

  • Portfolio demonstrating end-to-end design ability across brand-led initiatives with a focus on customer journey.

  • Deep knowledge of UX best practices, content strategy and hierarchy, and strategic thinking.

  • Hands-on experience with visual identity, wireframes, user flows, and prototyping.

  • Experience maintaining or evolving design systems and brand standards.

  • Refined visual and typographic sensibility with a dedication to craft, UI, and design excellence.

  • Strong organizational and project management skills across concurrent initiatives in a matrixed environment.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management across marketing, brand, UX, and product teams — with the ability to effectively present to and influence stakeholders.

  • Integration of AI tools in current workflows.

  • Expertise in design tools like Figma and Adobe Creative Suite.

  • BA/BS in Design, UX, HCI, or related field preferred.

About the Team:

The Finance team is responsible for global financial support in four key areas: Global Financial Operations (GFO), Financial Management Accounting (FMA), Tax and Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A). The team covers everything from back-office functions like payroll and customer billing to tax compliance and budget forecasting.

About the Role

The Consumer Finance team is seeking a Manager, FP&A to support the growth and performance of Dow Jones' subscription businesses, including The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, and Investor's Business Daily (IBD).

This role will partner closely with leaders across Marketing, Product, Data Science, and Circulation to plan, forecast, and optimize subscriber revenue.

You will help drive financial insights across the full subscriber lifecycle—from acquisition and promotional strategy to retention, pricing, and lifetime value—ensuring the business achieves its growth and profitability objectives.

You will develop forward-looking models, evaluate investment decisions, and provide actionable insights that inform strategic priorities.

You will be work in our Midtown Manhattan or Princeton, New Jersey office 3 days a week and report to the VP Finance.

You Will:

  • Partner with Consumer, Marketing, and Product teams to develop and manage budgets and forecasts for digital and print subscription revenue across Dow Jones brands.

  • Build and maintain subscriber-based financial models, including drivers such as acquisition volume, promotional offers, pricing step-ups, churn/retention, and lifetime value (LTV).

  • Collaborate with Growth and Paid Media teams to evaluate customer acquisition efficiency (CAC, Cost Per Order, payback, ROI) and optimize marketing investment.

  • Analyze the financial impact of pricing changes, promotional strategies, bundling, and new product initiatives.

  • Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to assess risks and opportunities related to subscriber growth, retention, and ARPU.

  • Produce monthly performance reporting, including variance analysis and trend insights across key subscription KPIs (net adds, churn, conversion, mix, yield).

  • Support month-end close processes with a focus on subscription revenue and related accruals.

  • Build business cases to support strategic initiatives such as product launches, offer testing, international expansion, or channel optimization. Partner with Data Science and Analytics teams to ensure alignment between financial forecasts and subscriber behavior trends.

  • Support ad-hoc analyses and strategic projects as needed

You Have:

  • 6–7 years of experience in Commercial Finance, FP&A, or related roles, preferably supporting subscription, direct-to-consumer, media, SaaS, or recurring revenue businesses.

  • Strong understanding of subscription economics, including acquisition funnels, churn/retention, ARPU, and lifetime value.

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field, or related experience (preferred).

  • Advanced Excel skills (complex modeling, scenario analysis) and proficiency with Google Sheets/Slides.

  • Experience with financial planning systems such as SAP and TM1 (preferred).

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate data into actionable business insights.

  • Experience building financial models to evaluate marketing investment, pricing, and product strategies.

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

  • Demonstrated initiative, strong work ethic, and collaborative mindset.

Host, What’s News

The Wall Street Journal is seeking a dynamic Host for What's News , one of our largest and most crucial franchises. You will be the face, voice, and driving personality behind the What's News brand. In this role, you will be the ultimate go-to guide for new audiences trying to navigate a noisy, high-volume news cycle across platforms, including the franchise newsletter.

The ideal candidate is a total news junkie with a sharp, conversational writing style and a passion for stepping out from behind the byline to connect with readers directly—extending your presence far beyond the inbox to span vertical video on social media, audio products, and in-person live events.

This role is based in New York.

You will:

  • Serve as the lead steward and recognizable host for the What's News brand, actively growing its footprint and cultivating a loyal, habit-driven community of readers and viewers.

  • Act as the ultimate news navigator for audiences, distilling complex global business, finance, and geopolitical stories into clear, engaging, and highly digestible takeaways.

  • Write and curate the daily What's News newsletter, infusing it with a distinct, approachable, and conversational authority that introduces new audiences to WSJ journalism.

  • Regularly host reporter-to-camera vertical videos, audio segments, and social media dispatches in close collaboration with the audio, social and Talent Lab and video teams.

  • Foster two-way relationships with our audience by hosting Live Q&As, and appearing at WSJ events.

  • Partner closely with audience teams to relentlessly experiment with new ways to turn serendipitous, top-of-funnel readers into loyal, paying WSJ subscribers through your personal brand.

You have:

  • 7+ years of experience in a fast-paced digital newsroom, with a deep understanding of what modern audiences want and need from a daily news product.

job.title: Lead Data Scientist, Newsroom Analytics
job.description:
The Wall Street Journal is seeking a Lead Data Scientist, Newsroom Analytics to drive our newsroom's audience-data strategy. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Newsroom Data, you will be embedded in one of the world's most influential newsrooms, working directly with newsroom coverage, audience, and product strategy teams on the decisions that shape how news is reported, prioritized, and delivered to millions of readers.

This is a highly autonomous and strategic role that demands both rigorous data science and sharp analytical instincts in equal measure. Working closely with editorial and audience leaders, you'll surface the right problems and own the full arc from solution design to adoption, building the metrics, models, and forecasts that teams rely on. This includes developing tools teams actually use, translating complex methodologies into clear recommendations, and consistently connecting your work to outcomes that matter: how readers discover, engage with, and return to WSJ journalism. Beyond your own output, you will serve as a technical anchor for the team, mentoring colleagues, establishing shared standards for analytical rigor, and proactively driving continuous improvements across our workflows. The ideal candidate seamlessly balances statistical rigor, strategic newsroom thinking, and a genuine investment in the people and practices around them.

This position will be based in our New York office.

You will:

  • Partner with our digital strategy, coverage and product teams to identify the highest-impact analytical opportunities, define the right questions, and shape the data science roadmap around problems that drive real newsroom outcomes.

  • Design and build predictive and explanatory models end-to-end, from feature engineering and validation through production, making principled tradeoffs between complexity and interpretability along the way.

  • Translate quantitative findings into clear, actionable recommendations for senior newsroom and business stakeholders, and partner with cross-functional teams to see those recommendations through to adoption.

  • Own the core metrics and measurement systems that newsroom teams rely on to evaluate performance and make editorial decisions, ensuring they are accurate, well-documented, and trusted.

  • Apply rigorous statistical thinking to measure real-world editorial and audience impact, drawing on causal inference and observational methods alongside controlled experimentation to isolate what's actually driving outcomes.

  • Mentor and develop junior data team members, establishing shared standards for rigorous, production-ready analysis and building the team's collective technical capability over time.

You have:

  • 5+ years of experience in data science, analytics, or applied machine learning, preferably in a media, publishing, or subscription-based environment.

  • Proven ability to own models end-to-end in a lean team setting, including scheduling, maintaining, and iterating on outputs using orchestration tools such as Airflow.

  • Strong proficiency in Python including feature engineering, model training, validation, and interpretation, with experience maintaining production-quality, reproducible code in Git.

  • Advanced SQL and hands-on experience with large-scale data warehouses (Snowflake/BigQuery) as well as ETL workflows/analytics engineering frameworks (dbt).

  • Experience applying causal inference and statistical methods to measure real-world outcomes from observational data.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to frame quantitative findings as clear business or editorial recommendations for senior non-technical stakeholders, and a demonstrated ability to influence decisions without direct authority.

  • Experience building models that influence content strategy, audience development, or consumer retention.

Standout candidates will have strengths in one or more areas of the following:

  • Experience with NLP or text analysis methods, including topic modeling, classification, or entity extraction applied to content data.

  • Familiarity with off-platform attribution and audience measurement, specifically modeling the relationship between distributed content, platform referrals, and downstream subscription or engagement outcomes.

  • Experience leveraging AI to democratize data and enable faster time-to-insight.

To apply, please submit a resume and a cover letter explaining how your skills, experience and interests align with the expectations of the role by July 28th. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage early submission as the position may be filled before the deadline.

The Journal’s reporters, editors, developers, and audio and visual journalists create important and impactful stories, firmly rooted in fact and adhering to the highest ethical standards. We report without fear or bias, and we maintain a proper sense of perspective, detachment and objectivity in our reporting.

job.title: Lead Writer, Live Markets
job.description:
Lead Writer, Live Markets (New York)

The Wall Street Journal is seeking a dynamic journalist to serve as the lead writer for our Live Markets blog, based in the New York headquarters at the heart of global finance.

The ideal candidate is fluent in stocks, bonds, commodities, currencies, and crypto, with the skills to translate complex Wall Street lingo into plain English for our highly educated audience. In this high-visibility role, you will anchor real-time coverage of the biggest shifts in business, finance, and the U.S. economy, marshalling the resources needed to document the market's winners and losers as news unfolds. You bring sharp wit, voice, and distinct personality to your writing—always grounded in the smart and authoritative tone our readers expect. You love that markets change rapidly, and you relish unraveling the mysteries beneath the numbers by portraying the real people who make, lose, and manage fortunes.

The successful candidate will combine hyper-organization with a calm demeanor under intense deadline pressure. You will be one of the leaders on our Live Markets product, working closely with editors and reporters across global bureaus to spot emerging trends, synthesize complex economic data, and experiment with non-text storytelling formats like interactive graphics and audio.

You will:

  • Lead real-time, live-blog coverage of the defining market events, economic reports, and corporate moves driving global finance each day, bringing flair and keen insight to the page.

  • Coordinate with reporters and editors across newsrooms to synthesize breaking news into clear, compelling, and authoritative market commentary.

  • Identify opportunities to tell original market stories readers can’t find anywhere else, using data, graphics, and sharp narrative hooks.

  • Help shape the voice, tone, and strategic direction of the Live Markets blog and daily markets coverage for a global audience.

You have:

  • At least five years of financial journalism experience, with a track record of covering markets, the economy, or corporate finance under intense deadline pressure.

  • The skills and instincts to jump on breaking news immediately, writing quickly, cleanly, and with an engaging, witty, yet professional voice.

  • High flexibility to pivot seamlessly between asset classes and economic themes based on news flow.

  • Deep comfort navigating complex financial data and using numbers to undergird fast-turn stories.

  • A keen sense of the Journal’s audience and a collaborative approach to working with cross-bureau teams and multi-format editors.

To apply, please submit your resume, a cover letter detailing how you would lead Live Markets coverage, and five examples of your best work by Friday, October 2nd. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and early submission is encouraged.

job.title: Markets Editor
job.description:
Editor, Markets

The Wall Street Journal is seeking an ambitious, high-energy editor to oversee coverage of financial markets, an area at the core of our newsroom that intersects with the biggest economic and business storylines.

You will guide a team of expert journalists as they chronicle how Americans, from Wall Street pros to everyday traders, are investing trillions of dollars–in stock, bonds, crypto or other assets. That can involve uncovering and explaining the reasons behind wild market swings, identifying trades that are hot and those that have gone cold, and spotlighting the people who are at the center of the action.

The successful candidate will be able to shepherd daily news at a fast pace, ensuring that major developments are reported with the analytical sweep and context necessary for stories to lead our site and be splashed on our front page. At the same time, you’ll develop a pipeline of high-impact, revelatory features – from profiles of key figures to stories that take us deep inside companies that matter to our readers.

There’s a rich reservoir of material to tap into. The market is as reliant as ever on the AI boom, with little margin for error. Investors are embracing risky bets, from loosely-regulated prediction markets to exotic options. The U.S. government has intervened in the bond market to counter growing unease about inflation and runaway federal debt.

Your responsibilities will include working with reporters to brainstorm and sharpen ideas, line editing their stories and coaching them on developing sourcing that will generate impactful scoops. Enthusiasm for visual storytelling and a willingness to experiment with video, audio and emerging platforms are essential for this role.

Markets have a profound impact on people, businesses and governments; this marquee coverage is central to our report and highly visible on all our platforms. We’re looking for someone who can elevate our work so that it reaches the broadest possible audience.

You will:

  • Drive the Journal’s coverage of markets news, managing a team of reporters at a high level

  • Develop ambitious feature story ideas with reporters and collaborate with newsroom stakeholders to orchestrate their publication

  • Line edit stories with the help of a deputy editor

  • Work with reporters to cultivate sources across the investing world, including traders and fund managers

  • Guide reporters to contribute incisive posts for WSJ Live Markets, our widely-read platform for real-time markets coverage and analysis

  • Collaborate with product and tech teams to develop products that put WSJ markets coverage on the map with a wider audience

You have:

  • At least 10 years of experience in business journalism and command of the dynamics of financial markets

  • Experience as a story editor, or strong writing skills if you haven’t edited before

  • A desire to cultivate talent and help reporters achieve their potential

  • The ability to analyze data quickly and tell complicated stories in creative ways

  • An entrepreneurial, collegial spirit

To apply, please send:

  • A cover letter

  • A resume

  • If applicable, five clips showcasing your range. Include a paragraph that explains why each story is notable and what it says about your skills.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage early submission as the position may be filled before the deadline of Friday, October 9th.

This position is based in New York and will report to Financial Editor Amol Sharma.

job.description:
The Wall Street Journal is looking for a photo editor to join the Business News and Features teams in New York. This team drives visual coverage for our corporate, real estate, manufacturing, retail, and consumer travel desks. The role requires strong creative photographic ideas, assigning and research. We are seeking an adaptable team player who can both cover a specific beat and support multiple coverage areas, stepping in as needed to manage department needs and maintain seamless coverage.

Photo Editors are responsible for producing a strong and dynamic quality of photography. Skills in how to create visuals for business coverage, including conceptual photo assigning, are recommended. Our content requires bold digital display on mobile and desktop platforms, and a thoughtful approach to print requirements. You will attend weekly bureau and art meetings, working closely with a group of editors, coverage chiefs, publishing and print editors, platform leads, section art directors, graphics, video and audience colleagues on breaking news, daily and enterprise coverage.

We are looking for a digitally-forward editor with sharp editorial judgment and journalistic integrity who can perform strong agency and social media research with speed and efficiency. A qualified candidate has at least three years experience in an editorial photo editing role. The photo position reports to a Managing Photo Editor. The role is based in our New York office.

You will:

  • Assign photography and run your own shoot production; commissioning original content, including shoots in WSJ’s in-house photography studio, as well as on location.

  • Produce photo coverage across breaking news, daily news and feature articles, collaborating with newsroom editors, visual colleagues, SEO and platform teams, as well as Bureau and section chiefs and your department manager.

  • Work in our publishing system to photo edit article builds. Combine different visual elements, anticipating photographic and other needs as stories develop in a fast-paced newsroom environment.

  • Work with the editing desk, platform and off-platform editors to execute and surface the work strategically across all platforms.

  • Assign photographers to stories - brainstorm creative photo solutions, produce the shoots (including security, travel, visa, releases, budget) and brief the photographer.

  • Promote a diverse and exciting group of photographers and subjects, with an eye to building new audiences for our journalism.

You have:

  • An enthusiasm for good journalism and current events, coupled with keen news judgment and ethics.

  • Fast digital editing skills and expertise working in a publishing system, quickly and efficiently under tight deadlines

  • Strong organizational and communication abilities

  • The drive to get ahead of the news, monitor social media, pitch ideas and follow leads

  • Experience working in a fast-paced news environment and collaborating across teams

  • Familiarity with audience data tools and strategies for encouraging readers to engage with digital content.

  • Deep knowledge of responsive design and best practices for building stories for mobile devices.
